topics.caution: The explanation or real_life_example could turn સ્વપ્નિલ opening the hospital window near a real મધપૂડો into an invitation for a child to open windows near hives at home, glossing over his own first reaction ('કરડશે તો ઉપાધિ') and the fact he shut the window when the bees came in.
topics.guidance: Keep the child's own caution in the explanation — he was curious from a safe distance with a દૂરબીન and closed the window when bees entered — and let real_life_example stay with watching insects from indoors, not with approaching a hive.

topics.caution: A literal reading could push a child to imitate સ્વપ્નિલ exactly — holding out a hand for a wild bee to land on, or tasting an unknown droplet ('મધનું ટીપું') found on their skin — treating a real insect sting risk and an unidentified substance as safe because the story's bee turned out friendly.
topics.guidance: The explanation should mark this as the story's special turn (many quiet mornings of just watching built the trust, and it is fiction/વિસ્મય, not a method) and should say plainly, in the child's own world, that a real bee should never be touched, provoked, or its area disturbed, and nothing found on skin from an insect should be tasted — real bees sting to defend themselves; recall or example prompts should not ask a child to try holding out a hand to a bee.

chapter_level.guidance: Across M2 and M3, keep સ્વપ્નિલ's bee-watching framed as observation through a window with a દૂરબીન and, in the one close moment, as the story's fictional turn — never as a how-to for approaching, touching, or feeding a real hive; the chapter's own line 'કરડશે તો ઉપાધિ' is the safety register to preserve.
